title: Fixed-beta two-sided Duhamel remainder bridge
question: After the compact-source endpoint third moment is available, what exact finite-time two-sided Duhamel remainder follows on the preregistered fixed-beta OS-mixture word class, and which orbit bound is still required for thermodynamic direct D and delta-D Cauchy?

setup.finite_volume_derivations: L_sigma=i[H_(Lambda,sigma),.]/hbar for sigma in {+,-,0}; tau_sigma(t)=exp(t L_sigma)

setup.mixture_seminorm: ||X||_(beta,#)^2=psi_(beta,0)(X*X)+psi_(beta,0)(XX*) on the support-reduced fixed-beta OS-mixture W-star envelope.

conditional_hypotheses.bounded_word_orbits: For 0<=s<=T, tau_sigma(s) and tau_0(s) preserve the declared word class and are beta,#-contractive.
conditional_hypotheses.second_orbit_bound: For each sigma, ||d^2/dt^2 [tau_sigma(t)(W_a)-tau_0(t)(W_a)]||_(beta,#) <= K_sigma(T) uniformly on 0<=t<=T.
conditional_hypotheses.initial_second_coefficient: At t=0 the bound supplied by the compact-source endpoint bridge is K_initial^4=(|a|/(hbar*chi))^4*C_force^4*w^3*M_bridge, with w=max(1,8/g).
conditional_hypotheses.orbit_extension: The all-time orbit hypothesis K_sigma(T)>=K_initial is not supplied by the static force moment; it is the named missing Duhamel input.
conditional_hypotheses.modular_commutation: If m commutes with both finite derivations on the word class, the same second-orbit argument applies to m R_sigma with a separate K_sigma_mod(T).

finite_time_theorem.modular_bound: ||m R_+(t)-m R_-(t)||_(beta,#) <= t^2*(K_+_mod(T)+K_-_mod(T))/2 when the modular commutation hypothesis holds.
finite_time_theorem.topology_consequence: This is a finite-member remainder precursor only; a volume-uniform net of these bounds would feed the existing direct two-sided mixture-L2 Cauchy criterion.

scope.not_closed: The orbit bound K_sigma(T), volume-uniform direct D and delta-D Cauchy, exhaustion, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, beta-independent dynamics, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
